summary: Christoph Harbsmeier is a sinologist and linguist who studied at Merton College, the University of Oxford, and the University of Copenhagen (Ph.D.). He held posts at Universiti Sains Malaysia and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1980.

Christoph Kleine is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Marburg and Bukkyo University, later holding professorships at the University of Munich (2004–2008) and the University of Leipzig (from 2008).

Christoph Theodosius Walther was an Indologist and linguist. He studied theology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1720 and served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission from around 1725 to 1739.

Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned his Dr. phil and habilitation at the University of Vienna, also studying at LSE under Bronisław Malinowski. He was a professor at Osmania University and SOAS University of London.

Christoph-Ernst Hauri was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Basel. He held posts at the universities of Geneva, Lausanne, Texas Health Science Center, Queensland, and Zurich, where he became a titular professor.

Christophe Jaffrelot is an Indologist who studied at Sciences Po under Jean Leca. He has held positions at Sciences Po, the CNRS from around 1991, and King's College London as Professor of Indian Politics and Sociology from around 2012.

Christophe Vielle is an Indologist. He has held academic posts including Research Professor at KU Leuven (attested 2009), professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013), and associate member at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Christopher Andreas Holmboe was a scholar of linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oslo and under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval, later serving as a professor at the University of Oslo (1825–1876).

Christopher Braider earned his PhD from Trinity College Dublin in 1982. He served as a lecturer and associate professor at Harvard University between 1983 and 1992, and became a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder in 2003.

Christopher Byrne is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015), where he studied under Grace S. Fong, G. Victor Sōgen Hori, and Robin D. S. Yates.

Christopher D. Emms specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has been a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University (attested 2026), studying under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke.

Christopher G. Framarin works in philosophy and Indology. He earned an M.A. at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and a Ph.D. at the University of New Mexico, and has held faculty posts at the University of Calgary.
Christopher Hatchell works in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Virginia, where he studied under academic mentor David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ohio State and Indiana University Bloomington under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, joining the Indiana University Bloomington faculty around 1978.

Christopher Isherwood was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Corpus Christi College and King's College London, studied under Swami Prabhavananda, and held a post at California State University, Los Angeles from around 1959 to 1962.

Christopher Ives is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He served as an assistant professor of religion at the University of Puget Sound (1987–1993) and as professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College around 2001.

Christopher Jon Jensen is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University, completing his PhD in 2018 under James A. Benn.
Christopher Kelley is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He was a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions in 1982 and Doshi Professor of Indic and Comparative Theology at Loyola Marymount University (attested 2001–2017).

Christopher L. Diamond specializes in Indology and archaeology. He studied at SOAS and the University of Washington under Heidi R. M. Pauwels, and held teaching roles at the University of Washington, University of Puget Sound, and University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2019.
